P8327:
A branch line from Jamestown to Ellendale, North Dakota, was described as part of the Bakken East Pipeline project. The Energy Information Administration listed about 90 miles of lateral pipe for this branch.{eia} A May 2026 article said it would serve the Applied Digital data center at Ellendale.{iir}

In May 2026 the company said that its open season brought no interest at the Ellendale location. The lateral is not in the current design or the updated map, which showed about 353 miles of main line and 21 miles of lateral pipe.{mdu} The line is now treated as cancelled.
P8124:
Columbia Gulf Transmission applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in November 2025 to build the Maysville Project. A notice from January 2026 sets the schedule for the environmental review.{fmay}

The project would add 42 miles of new 30-inch pipe in Rowan, Fleming and Mason Counties, Kentucky. It would end at a new meter station at the Spurlock Power Station.{fmay} It would carry 340,000 dekatherms per day.{pgjm} The Energy Information Administration lists a 2029 start and a cost of $400 million.{eia}
P8125:
Columbia Gulf Transmission filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on 15 October 2025 to build the Pulaski Project. It would add 41.3 miles of new 30-inch pipe from Lincoln County to a new South Somerset meter station in Pulaski County, Kentucky.{fpul}

The pipe would deliver 260,000 dekatherms per day to East Kentucky Power Cooperative's Cooper power station.{fpul} The same Energy Information Administration list gives this project a 2029 start and a $400 million cost.{eia}
P8126:
The Vicksburg Lateral was built to supply two power plants. A November 2000 notice describes about 37 miles of 20-inch pipe from the Columbia Gulf main line in Richland Parish, Louisiana, to the Baxter Wilson Plant and the proposed Warren Power Plant in Warren County, Mississippi. It would carry up to 285,000 dekatherms per day at an estimated cost of $20.1 million.{fvic}

The Energy Information Administration lists the lateral as completed in September 2001.{eia}
P8091:
Algonquin Gas Transmission applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in 2002 to build about 30 miles of 24-inch pipe across Massachusetts Bay, plus a 5-mile, 16-inch lateral to Deer Island. At the time the company was part of Duke Energy Gas Transmission.{ogjh}

A 2008 state mapping record describes the HubLine as built, about 29.5 miles long, mostly offshore between Beverly and Weymouth.{mass} The 24-inch size is the proposed one, and the as-built size has not been confirmed. No source confirms that the Deer Island lateral was built.
P8100:
In 2008 the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission authorized Bradwood Landing LLC and NorthernStar Energy LLC to build an LNG terminal on the Columbia River in Clatsop County, Oregon. The approval also covered 36.3 miles of pipeline to Northwest Pipeline in Cowlitz County, Washington.{ferb} A 2006 article confirms the length and a sendout of 1.3 billion cubic feet per day.{ogjb}

The terminal and pipeline were never built. No source gives a cancellation date, so the project is treated as cancelled.
P7837:
ONEOK, WhiteWater, MPLX and Enbridge announced the Eiger Express Pipeline on August 25, 2025. The approximately 450-mile, 42-inch pipeline is designed to carry up to approximately 2.5 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas from the Permian Basin in West Texas to the Katy area near Houston.{a_oneok} The Matterhorn joint venture owns 70% of the Eiger Express joint venture, and ONEOK and MPLX each own 15%. WhiteWater was to build and operate the pipeline.{a_oneok} The companies expected it to be finished in mid-2028, pending regulatory approvals.{a_oneok}

A Gattis Law project page said the partners reached a final investment decision in August 2025 and that construction and regulatory approvals were under way.{a_gattis_e}
P7834: The Mustang Mainline is the 178-mile segment of the Mustang Express Pipeline. It runs from the Katy Hub in Katy, Texas to Port Arthur, Texas.{a_arm}{a_chron} ARM Energy Holdings announced a final investment decision on the 42-inch Mustang Express Pipeline on October 9, 2025. The $2.3 billion project had an anchor shipper commitment from Sempra Infrastructure for its Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 project. ARM Energy was to build and operate it with Pacific Investment Management Company and co-investors. The pipelines have a total capacity of 2.5 billion cubic feet per day and were expected to be finished in late 2028 or early 2029.{a_arm}
P7835: The Cougar Lateral is a 55-mile segment of the Mustang Express Pipeline. It runs from the Tres Palacios Storage to the Katy Hub in Katy, Texas.{a_arm} A Houston Chronicle article from October 2025 placed Tres Palacios Storage in Bay City.{a_chron}
P7836: The Golden Triangle and Spindletop Storage Lateral is a three-mile segment of the Mustang Express Pipeline around Port Arthur, Texas.{a_arm}
P7106:
Tennessee Gas Pipeline built the Cumberland Pipeline to supply the Tennessee Valley Authority's new natural gas power plant at the site of the Cumberland Fossil Plant. The 30-inch pipeline is a 32-mile lateral. It starts at the company's existing 100 Line in Dickson County, Tennessee and ends at the power plant in Stewart County, Tennessee.{a_marc} Marcellus Drilling News reported in July 2026 that the roughly $235 million project was placed in service on May 26, 2026.{a_marc}

In October 2024 a federal appeals court panel temporarily halted two permits needed to start construction. The panel's order delayed the start of work through Dickson, Houston and Stewart counties until the court decided the case.{a_power}
P5516:
CE Pipeline LLC planned about 37 miles of 42-inch natural gas pipeline in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana. It would have served the proposed CE FLNG liquefied natural gas export terminal, which CE FLNG LLC also planned. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission announced an environmental review of both in a December 2013 notice.{a_fr} A 2013 Natural Gas Intelligence article said FERC approved the pre-filing request for the terminal and gave a pipeline length of 45 to 72 miles.{a_nga}

The Department of Energy said that on October 11, 2016 FERC ended its pre-filing review of the project because of a lack of progress. In January 2025 the department dismissed the pending part of the export application, noting that the company had not reported any concrete action in more than 12 years.{a_doe} No source shows that the pipeline was built.
P7850: Forza is a proposed Targa natural gas pipeline in the Delaware Basin. Targa Resources said Forza Pipeline LLC would build about 36 miles of 36-inch pipe from Lea County, New Mexico to near the Wildcat Junction Station in Winkler County, Texas.{b_forza_os} Forza would also lease 43 miles of capacity on the Bull Run Extension to reach the Waha hub.{b_forza_os} The open season notice said it would provide about 750,000 Dth/d of firm capacity.{b_forza_os} Targa announced the project in November 2025 and filed a certificate application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on December 3, 2025.{b_sec} In its quarterly report for the period ending June 2026, Targa said operations were expected to begin in the middle of 2028, pending regulatory approvals.{b_sec}
P7851: Buffalo Run is a Targa natural gas pipeline project in Texas. Targa announced it on September 30, 2025.{b_tpr} It has two parts. One is a new 35-mile pipeline linking several Targa plants in the Permian Midland. The other is the conversion of an existing 55-mile Targa pipeline to natural gas service, which would link Targa's Midland and Delaware systems.{b_tpr} Targa said the project would be completed in stages and be fully complete in early 2028.{b_tpr} The Energy Information Administration listed it as announced, at about 90 miles in total, with a 2028 in-service year.{b_eia}
P7852: Bull Run is an existing Targa intrastate natural gas pipeline in the Delaware Basin in Texas.{b_sec} The Energy Information Administration described it as Targa's existing 42-inch Bull Run Pipeline.{b_eia} Targa announced a 43-mile extension of it in August 2025.{b_sec}
P7853: Targa's announcements do not describe a Buffalo Run Extension separate from the Buffalo Run project. A November 2025 Targa investor presentation listed Buffalo Run at about 90 miles, to be completed by early 2028.{b_inv}
P7854: The Bull Run Extension is a Targa intrastate natural gas pipeline in the Delaware Basin. It would add about 43 miles of 42-inch pipe to the existing Bull Run pipeline, from Wildcat Junction Station in Winkler County, Texas to the Waha hub.{b_eia} Targa announced the extension in August 2025.{b_sec} A November 2025 investor presentation gave an in-service date of the first quarter of 2027.{b_inv} The Energy Information Administration said the extension would also carry the capacity leased to the Forza pipeline, and listed service as targeted for the second quarter of 2028.{b_eia}
P7109: The Targa Red Hills Interconnect is a lateral pipeline in New Mexico and Texas. In April 2024, Carlsbad Gateway, LLC asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for approval to build about 20 miles of 20-inch pipe.{b_fr} The line would run from the outlet of Targa's Red Hills Processing Plant in Lea County, New Mexico to an interconnection with the Agua Blanca Pipeline in Loving County, Texas.{b_fr} The notice said it would carry 350,000 dekatherms per day and cost an estimated $35 million.{b_fr}
P7861: The Residue Header is part of the Anadarko Gathering System owned by Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering), L.P., a Producers Midstream company. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission described it as a 150-mile pipeline of 16-inch and 20-inch diameter from Washita County, Oklahoma to Roberts County, Texas.{b_ferc} In June 2025, Producers Midstream said its Palo Duro Pipeline would use leased capacity on this header system as part of a new interstate service.{b_pm} The commission issued certificates for the project on March 19, 2026.{b_ferc}
P7862: The Palo Duro Gas Pipeline is an existing 16-inch pipeline of about 275 miles in Texas, from Nolan County to an interconnection with the header system in Wheeler County.{b_ferc} It is operated by Palo Duro Transmission L.P., a Producers Midstream company.{b_ferc} In June 2025, Producers Midstream announced plans to convert it to interstate service and began a binding open season.{b_pm} On March 19, 2026, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued certificates for the project.{b_ferc} The commission said the interstate service would use the northernmost 61 miles of the pipeline plus leased header capacity, for up to 80,000 Dth/d.{b_ferc} Palo Duro Transmission signed a binding agreement for all of that capacity with Scurry Downstream, LLC.{b_ferc}
P6900: The Cimarron River Pipeline is a natural gas pipeline of about 407 miles in Oklahoma and Kansas, operated by Cimarron River Pipeline, LLC.{b_rex} Rextag lists DCP Midstream, LP as the owner and a system capacity of 0.16 Bcf/d.{b_rex} It receives raw gas from gathering connections in the Anadarko Basin.{b_rex}
P7856:
Great Basin Gas Transmission Company owns and operates a natural gas pipeline system in Nevada. The company was formerly known as Paiute Pipeline Company and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Southwest Gas Corporation.{c_gb_home} In 1963, Southwest Gas built a new transmission line from the Idaho-Nevada border southwest across northern Nevada to the Carson City and Reno-Sparks area and Lake Tahoe.{c_gb_home} The system now extends from the Idaho-Nevada border to the Nevada-California border.{c_gb_home}

A company safety brochure describes the system as 900 miles long. It delivers gas to three local distribution companies and to large customers such as power plants, mines, and processing plants.{c_gb_safety} A June 2025 trade press report gave the length as 898 miles.{c_gb_pgj} These figures are for the whole system. No source gives a length for the main line alone.
P7857:
Great Basin applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on May 1, 2023 to build its 2024 Expansion Project in Nevada.{c_gb_fr23} The project has three parts. Great Basin would build about 0.25 miles of 20-inch pipeline loop along its Carson Lateral in Storey County. It would replace about 2.88 miles of 10-inch pipe with 20-inch pipe along the Carson Lateral in Lyon County. It would also build about 0.28 miles of 12-inch pipeline loop on its South Tahoe Lateral in Douglas County.{c_gb_fr23}

The project would provide 5,674 dekatherms per day of added firm transportation service for two existing shippers. Great Basin estimated the cost at $14,939,850.{c_gb_fr23} A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice dated November 28, 2023 said staff had prepared an environmental assessment of the project.{c_gb_ea23} No source found confirms final approval or construction.
P7858:
Great Basin applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on September 29, 2025 to install about 33 miles of new pipeline and abandon about 21 miles of its existing Gabbs Lateral in Nevada. The Gabbs Lateral Naval Air Station Fallon Relocation Project would start about 26 miles east of Schurz and end about 3 miles west-northwest of Gabbs.{c_gb_mci}

A Federal Register notice dated March 13, 2026 said Commission staff had prepared an environmental assessment. It described about 32.6 miles of new pipe, made up of 18.8 miles of 8-inch pipe and 13.8 miles of 6-inch pipe. It also described removing about 21.2 miles of existing pipe. The notice said the project would not provide any incremental capacity.{c_gb_ea26g} Great Basin said construction was scheduled to begin on or about March 1, 2027 and be completed by November 1, 2027, subject to approvals.{c_gb_mci}
P7859:
Great Basin applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on April 15, 2025 to build its 2026 Expansion Project in Lyon and Washoe Counties, Nevada. The project would install about 2.32 miles of new 20-inch pipeline loop along the Carson Lateral, and replace about 2.35 miles of existing 10-inch pipe with new 20-inch pipe.{c_gb_fr25} It would add 8,129 dekatherms per day of firm transportation capacity for two existing shippers in northern Nevada and northern California. Great Basin estimated the cost at $18,884,092.{c_gb_fr25}

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice dated November 25, 2025 said staff had prepared an environmental assessment. It described about 4.7 miles of upsized or looped pipeline in two segments.{c_gb_ea25} No source found shows that the project was approved or built.
P7860:
Great Basin proposed a 2028 Expansion Project to add natural gas capacity in northern Nevada. It opened a binding open season on January 28, 2025 for firm service starting as early as November 1, 2028. The closing date was extended to May 28, 2025.{c_gb_pgj} Southwest Gas Holdings announced on June 5, 2025 that the open season had closed with strong interest. It estimated about 1.25 billion cubic feet per day of new capacity and a cost of $800 million to $1.2 billion.{c_gb_pgj}

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission scoping notice dated April 27, 2026 described about 195 miles of new 42-inch pipeline and about 15 miles of new 24-inch lateral pipelines. The project would include a new Jungo Road Compressor Station. Great Basin planned to abandon about 142 miles of existing pipeline, mostly from the 1960s, plus the Rye Patch and Lovelock Compressor Stations.{c_gb_fr26} A company fact sheet gave about 230 miles of pipeline, up to about 948,000 dekatherms per day of new capacity, and a target in-service date of November 2028.{c_gb_fact} A December 2025 letter to the Commission, reported by Nevada Current in June 2026, described 181 miles of new pipeline plus a 14 mile segment, running from near Winnemucca to west of Fernley.{c_gb_nv} The sources differ on the length and the capacity. The project was in planning and development as of 2026.{c_gb_fact}
P6895:
A 2021 open season notice from Equitrans, L.P. described its Mainline system as a natural gas transmission and storage system in north central West Virginia, southwestern Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio. Equitrans, L.P. is a subsidiary of Equitrans Midstream Corporation.{c_eq_open} EQT Corporation acquired Equitrans Midstream in a merger, and EQT's results include the acquired assets from July 22, 2024.{c_eq_eqt}

The sources give figures for the whole transmission and storage system and not for the Mainline alone. As of December 31, 2022, the system included about 940 miles of interstate pipelines regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. Its total throughput capacity was about 4.4 Bcf per day.{c_eq_trans}
P6896:
EQT Midstream Partners announced on October 13, 2016 that it had acquired the Allegheny Valley Connector transmission and storage system from EQT Corporation for $275 million in cash. The acquisition was effective October 1, 2016.{c_eq_avc} The system includes about 209 miles of transmission pipeline and 11 Bcf of working gas storage capacity. It has 450 MMcf per day of transmission capacity.{c_eq_avc} The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission regulates it.{c_eq_avc} In September 2015 Equitrans asked the Commission to restate the certificated storage capacity of the system to 11.2 Bcf of working gas, down from 15.1 Bcf.{c_eq_fr15}

A May 2019 notice described plans to replace about 3.85 miles of 20-inch pipe on the TP-4555 pipeline, which is part of the Allegheny Valley Connector System, with about 3.92 miles of new 20-inch pipe in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania.{c_eq_fr19} In January 2026 Equitrans asked to abandon in place the West Fairfield Compressor Station. It said the station was no longer needed to meet its firm obligations on the system.{c_eq_fr26}
P6897:
Equitrans, L.P. filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on December 30, 2014 to build the Ohio Valley Connector Project in West Virginia and Ohio. It proposed 50 miles of pipeline and 36,000 horsepower of compression. The project would provide up to 850,000 dekatherms per day of added firm transportation service. Equitrans estimated the cost at $416.00 million and proposed an in-service date of June 2016.{c_eq_ovc15} An earlier notice from September 2014 described 34 miles of 30-inch pipeline, 1.5 miles of 30-inch pipeline, and 14 miles of 24-inch loop.{c_eq_ovc14}

An October 2016 company release said the pipeline began transportation service on October 1, 2016 from northern West Virginia to Clarington, Ohio. It described the pipeline as a 37-mile extension. EQT held a 20-year agreement for 650 MMcf per day of firm capacity on it.{c_eq_ovc16} In January 2022 Equitrans applied for an Ohio Valley Connector Expansion Project to provide up to 350,000 dekatherms per day of added deliverability.{c_eq_ovc22} Equitrans Midstream expected to spend about $40 million in 2024 to complete that expansion.{c_eq_etrn}
P7999:
TC Energy announced the Appalachia Supply Project in its first quarter 2026 results, released on May 1, 2026. The project expands the Columbia Gas system and is designed to provide up to 0.8 Bcf/d of capacity for new gas-fired power generation.{d_tc} The company estimated the cost at about US$1.5 billion and gave an anticipated in-service date of 2030.{d_tc} Oil & Gas Journal reported in May 2026 that the project is backed by a 20-year take-or-pay contract with an investment-grade utility. It said the project can be expanded to 2 Bcf/d with added compression and minor modifications.{d_ogj}

The announcements did not give a pipeline length, pipe diameter or route.
P7855:
The South System Expansion 4 Project was developed by Southern Natural Gas Company and its affiliate Elba Express Company. Southern Natural Gas is equally owned by subsidiaries of Kinder Morgan and Southern Company, and Elba Express is a Kinder Morgan subsidiary.{d_fs} The companies began the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission pre-filing process on October 30, 2024 and filed a certificate application on June 30, 2025.{d_fs} The project adds about 1.3 Bcf/d of firm capacity on the Southern Natural Gas South Main Line, at an estimated cost of about $3.5 billion.{d_fs}

The project is almost entirely looping and compression additions on existing assets. A Kinder Morgan fact sheet gave about 290 miles of looping, mainly 42-inch, 36-inch and 30-inch pipe.{d_fs} Pipeline & Gas Journal reported in August 2026 that the plan has 22 loops totaling about 291 miles across Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia.{d_pg} The commission approved the project on July 31, 2026.{d_pg}{d_kp} Kinder Morgan expects the first phase to enter service in the fourth quarter of 2028 and the second phase in the fourth quarter of 2029.{d_kp} A 2025 fact sheet had anticipated construction starting in the fourth quarter of 2026.{d_fs}
P8377:
Southern Natural Gas Company announced a binding open season for the Southeast Connector Project on September 16, 2026. The open season closed on October 7, 2026.{d_nt} The project adds a new supply line that would take gas in Tennessee from four pipelines. It also expands the Southern Natural Gas system in Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina and Florida.{d_nt} The notice gave a target in-service date of November 1, 2030, with all service starting no later than November 1, 2032.{d_nt}

Kinder Morgan reported in October 2026 that Southern Natural Gas had made a final investment decision on the project. The project is designed to carry up to 2.6 Bcf/d through about 470 miles of new pipeline plus new and expanded compression.{d_sec} Service is expected to start in phases from the fourth quarter of 2030, subject to permits and approvals. Kinder Morgan put its own share of the cost at $3.1 billion.{d_sec} WPLN News reported in October 2026 that about 150 of the 470 miles are in Tennessee, running from Sumner County to Marion County. It gave the pipe diameter as 48 inches and said capacity could grow to 3.5 Bcf/d.{d_wp}
P6533: TC Energy describes the Columbia Gulf Transmission Pipeline as a system stretching 3,367 miles. It connects to virtually every major pipeline on the U.S. Gulf Coast and to additional Midwestern lines.{d_cg} TC Energy says the natural gas that heats homes and businesses in Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee and Kentucky is often supplied by the pipeline.{d_cg} It is regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.{d_cg}
P7149: The Weizhou Weibei Gas Pipeline is part of the Guangxi Gas Pipeline Network in China. It has an onshore section and a subsea section. The diameter and design pressure figures refer to the onshore section only. Data for the subsea section was not available.
P7654: The Nanning-Fusui Branch is part of the Guangxi Gas Pipeline Network in China. No source gave an explicit commissioning date. The 2023 start year is inferred from the date the construction was completed.{w83}
P7662:
The Guangxi Development and Reform Commission approved the Guilin-Yangshuo-Lipu natural gas branch pipeline on 17 July 2019.{w84} The approval names Guangxi Guangtou Natural Gas Pipeline Network Co as the project company. It covers about 100 km of new pipe, with about 50 km in Linwei district, 32 km in Yangshuo county and 18 km in Lipu county.{w84}

The approved design flow is 172 million cubic meters a year at 4 MPa, using pipe of 273.1 mm diameter. Total investment was put at about 346.04 million yuan. The approval lapses if construction does not start within two years, unless an extension is granted.{w84}
P7099: The Gulf of Guinea Gas Pipeline is a proposed link between Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea.{w85} No route for it has been found on maps. Route data may become available as construction progresses and more detailed engineering plans are released.
P8351:
Gazprom Mezhregiongaz announced this inter-settlement gas pipeline on 27 April 2021. It runs through the Nazyvaevsk district of Omsk Oblast and serves Loris-Melikovo, Bogodukhovka, Cheremnovka, Kochkovatka, Spassk, Fomikha and the Kochkovatsky siding. The announced length was 49.6 kilometers, with about 5 kilometers already laid. Completion was planned for the fourth quarter of 2021. The pipeline is part of the Omsk 2021 to 2025 gasification program.{w96}

Governor Khotsenko reported that the pipeline was commissioned on 20 June 2025. It supplies 521 households and 6 boilers. The regional gas company Oblgaz built it jointly with Gazprom.{w97}{w98} The 2025 coverage gave the same 49.6 kilometers as the 2021 announcement.
P8375:
The Yurkharovskoye field is connected to the Yamburg to Urengoy trunk gas pipeline by a pipeline 51 kilometers long. A Neftegaz.ru field page gives this figure. The field has produced since 2003, and the license is held by NOVATEK-Yurkharovneftegaz, which is wholly owned by Novatek.{w112}

A 2006 article written before the second stage of development described a second line of 20 billion cubic meters a year from the field to the trunk line, 52 kilometers long. It is unclear whether this is a separate pipe from the 51 kilometer line. The sources do not give a diameter or start year, and no route was found.
P7633: The Northeast Branch of the National Petroleum and Natural Gas Pipeline Network Group proposed the Daqing-Changling gas pipeline in China. The project appears in notices on the group's website.{w113} Two later notices from the same site also cover the project.{w114}{w115}
P7655: The Xingye Branch is part of the Guangxi gas pipeline network in China. No source states when the branch was commissioned. It is treated as operating because a completion date in 2023 was reported.{w116}
P7674: The Luzhai Branch is part of the Guangxi gas pipeline network in China. No source states when the branch was commissioned. It is treated as operating because a completion date in 2022 was reported.{w117}
P8331:
Gazprom is working on a gas pipeline in Russia from the Aganskaya compressor station in Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug to the Vertikos compressor station in the north of Tomsk Oblast. In a reply to the news agency RIA Tomsk on 23 June 2025, the Tomsk vice-governor said the line would be more than 400 kilometers long. He gave 2029 as the target date and said it would raise the capacity of the Nizhnevartovsk-Parabel-Kuzbass route.{w118}

Interfax reported in April 2025 on a Gazprom board presentation. Laser scanning was done and engineering surveys were being completed for the Aganskaya to Aleksandrovskaya stretch.{w119} Neftegaz places that stretch inside Gazprom's Eastern Gas Supply System. It would link existing trunk lines to supply Altai, Kemerovo, Novosibirsk and Tomsk.{w120} No tender, final investment decision or permit was found. No capacity, diameter, cost or route was found.
P8335:
Gazprom gazoraspredelenie Tomsk is building a gas pipeline of about 112 kilometers in Novosibirsk Oblast, Russia. It runs from the Cherepanovo gas distribution station to Suzun and would serve nine settlements under the oblast's 2021-2025 gasification program. The company press service said construction began in October 2024.{w121}

In March 2025 the regional ministry said 40 kilometers had been built and that completion was expected in 2026.{w122} No later report was checked, so the line may be finished by now. Diameter, pressure, capacity and route were not found.
P8339:
Gazprom is building the Galich-Manturovo-Sharya gas pipeline in Kostroma Oblast, Russia. It is a branch of about 182 kilometers from the gas distribution station at Galich to the one at Sharya. It is built in four stages: Galich to Parfenyevo at 55.3 kilometers, Parfenyevo to Neya at 26.3, Neya to Manturovo at 57.7, and Manturovo to Sharya at 42.8.{w123} Construction began in 2011, was paused in 2013 and resumed in 2020.

Gas reached Parfenyevo in 2021. It reached the Neya and Manturovo stations in December 2023.{w124} The last stage, Manturovo to Sharya, was due in the third quarter of 2024. In July 2026 the Kostroma regional press reported a governor's review that put the gas launch at Sharya at the end of 2026.{w125} A project page gives the budget as 7.4 billion rubles.{w126} Diameter and pressure were not found on any verified page.
P8343:
This line carries gas from the Moscow Region gas ring to KRP-13 in the Molzhaninovsky district of Moscow. A 2010 Moscow government decree lists it as 26.8 kilometers long and 1,020 millimeters wide. The same decree notes an older reserve string of 800 millimeters, whose length it does not give.{w127} KRP-13 itself has been in service since 1963.{w128}

The Kryukovskoe division of Gazprom transgaz Moskva lists the pipelines to KRP-13 and KRP-14 among the lines it built, commissioned and operates.{w129} The 2010 decree has since lapsed, and no later source repeats the length.
P8348:
This pipeline runs from the Voskresensk compressor station to KRP-11 in the Moscow area. A 2010 Moscow government decree lists it as 98.6 kilometers long and 1,020 millimeters wide. The decree says Voskresensk supplies KRP-11, KRP-15 and KRP-16, and that KRP-11 has been in service since 1957.{w127}

Gazprom transgaz Moskva reported in 2015 on the reconstruction of KRP-16. It names the line as the Voskresensk to KRP-11 trunk and says a second inlet of 660 meters to KRP-16 was built off it.{w130}{w131} The length comes only from the 2010 decree, which has lapsed. A 2019 Moscow scheme lists no KRP-11 among its sources. The KRP-16 line may share a corridor with this one, so the two lengths should not be added.
P8352:
Gazprom built the Mozdok-Grozny gas pipeline from the Mozdok compressor station in North Ossetia-Alania to the Grozny gas distribution station in Chechnya. A Gazprom Transgaz Stavropol release of 11 December 2020 said construction was complete. It described a line over 100 kilometers long with a diameter of 720 millimeters. It said the line tied into the Mozdok-Nevinnomyssk and Novopskov-Aksai-Mozdok pipelines.{w132}

A Gazprom press release of 7 April 2021 reported the opening in Grozny. The line is 101.7 kilometers long and follows the same corridor as the Stavropol-Grozny pipeline. It has 13 road crossings and 6 water crossings, including the Terek River. It supplies the Grozny thermal power plant of 360 megawatts and the Grozny gas distribution station.{w133} The news site EADaily repeated the report.{w134} A federal territorial planning scheme also lists the line.{w108} No source giving the start of construction was verified.
P8356:
The Obkhod-Shakhunya gas pipeline is a high-pressure line between settlements in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, Russia. It runs from the gas distribution station near Obkhod village in the Urensky municipal okrug to Shakhunya. The governor reported its completion to President Putin by video link on 18 September 2026.{w135} The regional government gave the length as 30.6 kilometers.{w136}{w137}

Earlier regional figures from December 2024 and January 2026 list a separate 30 kilometer branch to the Obkhod station. They list this line separately as a 32 kilometer line from Obkhod to Shakhunya. Capacity, diameter and cost were not found.
P8360:
The Rybinsk-Okhotino gas pipeline in Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia, runs from the third gas distribution station in Rybinsk to Okhotino. It crosses the Rybinsk and Myshkino districts. Gazprom Mezhregiongaz carried out the project under the Gazprom 2021-2025 gas supply and gasification program. Neftegaz reported that construction began in August 2021 and gave the length as 42.5 kilometers.{w138}

Gazprom gazoraspredelenie Yaroslavl and Rybinskgazservis commissioned the line on 7 September 2023. Their announcement gave the built length as 43 kilometers, rounded.{w139} Diameter, capacity and cost were not found.
P8364:
Gazprom is building a gas pipeline branch to the town of Soligalich in Kostroma Oblast, Russia. The customer is Gazprom transgaz Ukhta and the contractor is Gazstroyproekt.{w140} The branch is 63.8 kilometers long and 300 millimeters wide, with a design pressure of 7.4 megapascals. It ties into the Ukhta-Torzhok trunk at kilometer 848.65. According to a trade publication, it entered state expert review in late 2022.{w141}

An earlier project listing said completion was planned for the end of 2025. A letter page dated 2 July 2026 reports that Gazprom group organizations were building the branch, a connecting line to the town, and the town street network. It said 53 percent of the street network was laid and that completion was planned for 2026.{w142} Completion has not been confirmed. No route was found.
P8368:
The Sakha Republic and Sakhatransneftegaz signed a concession agreement for gas supply to the left bank of the Vilyuy River on 3 September 2026. Under the agreement, works would start in October 2026 and gas would reach Dyullyukyu in August 2028. All work would be finished by the end of 2029. The project includes an underwater crossing of the Vilyuy.{w143}

In February 2025 the head of the republic gave the length of the first stage, from Tamalakan to Dyullyukyu, as 32 kilometers. A branch to Dyullyukyu would be added to it.{w144} Capacity, diameter and route were not found.
P8372:
Gazprom Transgaz Sankt-Peterburg operates a gas pipeline branch from the Valday area to the gas distribution station at Borovichi in Novgorod Oblast, Russia. A Gazprom procurement notice of 10 June 2021 names the object as the gas pipeline branch to the Borovichi station. It covers a design for partial liquidation of a 1.6 kilometer section with a diameter of 250 millimeters.{w145} A government order of 31 January 2017 calls the existing line the Valday-Borovichi-2 trunk gas pipeline.{w146}

A map entry on OpenStreetMap shows the line at 530 millimeters, run by Gazprom transgaz Saint Petersburg.{w147} No source states the length, the start date, the capacity or the cost.
P8376:
Gazprom transgaz Surgut built a gas offtake in Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug, Russia, from the Yuzhno-Balykskaya compressor station to Nefteyugansk. It supplies two new gas distribution stations, Karkateevy at 79,000 cubic meters per hour and Pyt-Yakh at 42,000 cubic meters per hour. Neftegaz reported the launch on 17 September 2026 and described an offtake of more than 47 kilometers.{w148} The news site Faktologia gave the total as 47.3 kilometers including the pipelines to the new stations.{w149}

A Neftegaz report from 2021, based on the Glavgosexpertiza review, gave a diameter of 250 millimeters and a pressure of 7.4 megapascals. It gave a design length of about 44.3 kilometers, so the built length differs.{w150} No route was found.
P7845: CPC proposed the Tungsiao-Datan offshore gas pipeline in Taiwan.{w151} It appears to be part of the larger Taichung-Tunghsiao-Datan offshore gas pipeline project. A row for the whole project may overlap this segment.
P7656: This 9 km segment of the Guangxi gas pipeline network links the Sinopec Nanning Station with the Zhongran Gate station. The sources found give no explicit commissioning date. The operating status is inferred from the completion date.
P8332:
The Anapa to Taman gas pipeline runs about 106 km in Krasnodar Krai. Two reports from May and June 2023 describe it as part of the Southern Gas Transport Corridor and say it entered service in 2016.{w152}{w153} Both reports repeat the same story about the state expert review of the project.

A Gazprom Transgaz Krasnodar press release from February 2025 calls it an existing line operated by that company. The release says a second string was being laid alongside it.{w154} No capacity or diameter for the existing line was found. The 7.5 billion cubic meters per year in some sources is the figure for the expanded project.
P8340:
Gazprom Gazoraspredelenie Ivanovo began building a 40.3 km inter-settlement gas pipeline in the Gavrilovo-Posadsky district of Ivanovo Oblast in 2021. A Gazprom Mezhregiongaz release from July 2021 said the line would serve 1,098 households and four boiler houses in villages including Zakomelye, Yarshevo and Yardenikha. It gave 2022 as the planned completion year.{w159}

A regional television report from May 2023 said the pipeline from Gavrilov Posad had been built, was more than 40 km long, passed through 10 settlements, and had brought gas to Zakomelye.{w160} No source gives the exact commissioning date.
P8344:
Gazprom built a gas branch in Astrakhan Oblast from the Makat to North Caucasus trunk line to Khosheutovo, Volnoye and Kharabali. The project followed a 2012 agreement between Gazprom and the Astrakhan regional government. The first weld was made on 16 September 2016. The line uses 500 mm steel pipe and is about 79.6 km long, and it includes three gas distribution stations.{w161}

About 79 km had been laid by October 2017. A July 2022 article from the Kharabali district said Gazprom fully completed construction of the branch in 2021.{w162} The exact year it entered service is approximate. No source states the capacity.
P8349:
A Moscow city government decree of 24 August 2010 describes seven radial trunk gas pipelines from the KGMO gas ring to stations called KRP. One of them is the line to KRP-16, listed at 87.8 km and 1,020 mm. The decree says the Voskresensk compressor station supplies KRP-11, KRP-15 and KRP-16, and that KRP-11, KRP-16 and KRP-17 have no reserve line.{w127}

A Gazprom Transgaz Moskva news item from February 2015 says KRP-16 was rebuilt and fed by a second DN1000 input off the Voskresensk to KRP-11 line. It places KRP-16 under the operational responsibility of Gazprom Transgaz Moskva.{w163} The start point given here is the supplying compressor station, not a surveyed tap point. No capacity, cost or feeder commissioning year was found. The KRP-11 line may share a corridor with this one, so the two lengths should not be added.
P8353:
Gazprom Transgaz Makhachkala built a new 29.3 km gas pipeline of 325 mm pipe in Dagestan to supply Novolakskoye and the Novolaksky and Khasavyurt districts. It replaced a 159 mm branch from 1986.{w164} The construction was done in 2024.{w165}

A company statement of 26 June 2025 reported the reconstruction as complete, and four Dagestan news outlets repeated it.{w166} The exact commissioning date is not stated, and the point where the branch leaves the main trunk was not identified.
P8357:
This 31 km inter-settlement gas pipeline in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast runs from the Obkhod gas distribution station in the Urensky district to Tonkino. It is part of a regional gasification programme backed by Gazprom.

In January 2026 the regional energy minister told a committee of the Legislative Assembly that the line was 39.7 percent complete. Works were planned to finish in 2026, with commissioning in 2027.{w167} A second outlet reported the same briefing.{w110} No source found names the legal owner. No capacity, diameter or cost was found, and no later status report has been found.
P8361: A 2016 profile of Arcticgas reported that in 2012 a 46 km pipeline was built to connect the gas treatment unit at the Samburgskoye field to the Unified Gas Supply System. It was built alongside the field start-up in April 2012.{w168} The profile does not name the pipeline owner, the diameter, the capacity, or the point where it joins the trunk system. No primary company page for the pipeline was found.
P8369: A 2022 Neftegaz report based on a Gazprom press release said a gas pipeline branch from Tomsk to Asino, plus a gas distribution station at Asino, was built between 2017 and 2022. The report gave the branch length as more than 78 km.{w176} No start year, diameter or capacity was found, and the operator was not confirmed.
P8373: Rosneft built a 108 km trunk pipeline from the Vankor field in Krasnoyarsk Krai to the Khalmerpayutinskoye field in Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug as part of the Vankor gas program. Rosneft press releases from 2017 and 2022 give the length and say the line was built.{w177}{w178} The 2017 release also says commercial gas from Vankor has gone into the Unified Gas Supply System since April 2014.{w177} No source states the start year of the pipeline itself, its diameter or its capacity.
P8346:
The Kuban to Crimea gas pipeline was commissioned on 27 December 2016, when Vladimir Putin started it by video link. It reached scheduled operation by early 2017.{w179} It runs from the Taman peninsula across the Kerch Strait in two strings to Crimea, then to Sevastopol, with a 27.3 km branch to Simferopol.{w180}

The operator announced a length of 358.7 km, which includes the strait crossing and the branch.{w181} A 2016 design review gave about 314 km, and other reports give about 400 km. The main line is 700 mm and the two branches are 500 mm.{w182} Chernomorneftegaz is named as the project customer and Stroygazmontazh as the builder. Planned throughput was 2.2 billion cubic meters per year, expandable to 4.4.
P7646: This segment runs from Bozhou to Huainan in Anhui Province, China, as part of the Wen 23 gas storage to Anqing pipeline. Its route closely overlaps the Anhui West branch line of the second Sichuan to Shanghai gas pipeline, which was expected to start operating in 2026. To avoid building twice, the project would use the Anhui West branch line for this stretch.{w183} The project would also rebuild and expand the Fuyang offtake and pipeline cleaning station on the Anhui West branch line.{w183}
P7660:
Guangxi Gas Group was named as the owner of this proposed branch in Hezhou. The project would lie in Babu District, Zhongshan County, Pinggui District and Fuchuan Yao Autonomous County in Hezhou, and in Zhaoping County and Mengshan County in Wuzhou. It would add three offtake stations at Xindu, Fuchuan and Zhaoping, and two valve chambers.{w184}

The project description called for a new DN273 gas pipeline in three sections. The Fuchuan section would be 39.6 kilometers long with a design pressure of 4.0 megapascals and a design flow of 20 million cubic meters a year. The Zhaoping section would be 29.3 kilometers long at 4.0 megapascals and 30 million cubic meters a year. The Xindu section would be 2.2 kilometers long at 6.3 megapascals and 65 million cubic meters a year. Total investment was given as 298.88 million yuan.{w184}
P8337:
Construction of the Elizovo to Vilyuchinsk gas pipeline was announced on 3 September 2026 at the Eastern Economic Forum, by Gazprom deputy chairman Markelov and the regional governor, Solodov. The pipeline would be buried and have a 426 millimeter diameter and a design flow of about 27,000 cubic meters an hour.{w186}

It would run from the Sosnovka area in Elizovsky District to the Rybachy residential district of Vilyuchinsk, skirting Krasheninnikov Bay.{w187} It would supply the municipal boiler houses of Vilyuchinsk and 12 Ministry of Defense boiler plants. No completion date or cost was found.
P8341:
A branch pipeline of about 26 kilometers was built to carry gas to and from the Kaliningrad underground gas storage facility. Two Russian reports on the opening of the storage describe it as a branch built for injection and withdrawal. A neftegaz.ru report from July 2016 is one of them.{w188} The other is a Gazprom-linked news item.{w189}

Construction ran from 2008 to 2012, and the storage was commissioned in 2016. Gazprom is the likely owner, based on its role as operator of the storage. The tie-in point on the trunk line, the diameter, the capacity and the start year were not found.
P8345:
Commercial gas from the Kirinskoye field, offshore Sakhalin, goes through a 139 kilometer pipeline to the Sakhalin compressor station. That station is the head station of the Sakhalin to Khabarovsk to Vladivostok gas system. The field began producing in 2014, with first gas in October 2013, and is operated by Gazprom Dobycha Shelf Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk.{w190}

The same article, from September 2026, says the field's treatment complex is being expanded for the Yuzhno-Kirinskoye field, with a full launch in 2028. That work includes new pipelines, among them a separate gas pipeline to the Sakhalin compressor station that is under construction. The pipe diameter, capacity and start date were not found.
P8350:
Gazprom specialists commissioned a gas pipeline between settlements in Kirov Oblast in December 2022. It was built under the Kirov Oblast gas supply and gasification program for 2021 to 2025. A Vyatka state broadcaster report of 24 December 2022 describes it as running from Kumeny to Vichevshchina, to serve Bolshoy Perelaz, Gorodchiki, Zhelny, Beltyugi, Verkhobystritsa and Bereznik. It said the line would serve about 400 households and 7 boiler houses.{w191}

A Kirov Oblast government release, reported on 12 January 2023, called it the longest pipeline between settlements in the oblast. The first households at Bolshoy Perelaz were connected that day.{w192} The diameter, capacity and cost were not found.
P8354:
The Nyuksenitsa to Arkhangelsk gas trunk line takes gas from Nyuksenitsa in Vologda Oblast to Arkhangelsk and Severodvinsk. It is operated by Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta, through its Nyuksenskoe linear production department.

A Pravda Severa article from September 2015 gave the linear length of the trunk line to Arkhangelsk and Severodvinsk as 796.9 kilometers. That figure includes branches to Velsk, Plesetsk, Mirny, Arkhangelsk, Severodvinsk and Novodvinsk.{w193} An industry news item from about 2005 gave construction markers of kilometers 0 to 147 for the start-up complex and 147 to 374 for the Plesetsk section. That implies a main line of about 374 kilometers, though no total length was stated.{w194} No diameter, capacity, start year or route was found.
P8358:
Gazprom is resuming a project to link the KS-3 Obskaya and KS-4 Yarsaltinskaya compressor stations. A URA.news article of 28 September 2026 described two lines of about 39 kilometers each. Gazprom Invest is the customer.{w195}

The tender for engineering surveys was run again in March 2026, and its value was cut to 1.097 billion rubles. A public discussion was set for 25 September to 24 October 2026.{w195} The project is at the survey stage. No construction contract or investment decision was reported. The article gave no capacity, diameter or cost for the lines.
P8362:
The Shakhunya to Tonshaevo gas pipeline is part of a regional gasification program for northern districts of Nizhny Novgorod Oblast. The governor, Nikitin, and Gazprom chief executive Miller signed the program in 2021.

At a meeting of a Legislative Assembly committee on 21 January 2026, the regional energy minister, Kurenkov, said construction was 38.4 percent complete. Commissioning was planned for 2027.{w167}{w110} On 23 September 2026 the governor said Tonshaevo was to be gasified the following year. An article from Gipernn, citing Kommersant-Privolzhye, gave the design period as 2025 to 2026 and reported that gasification dates for the northern districts had been pushed back.{w196} The capacity, diameter, cost and route were not found.
P8366:
The second string of the gas pipeline branch to the Starodub gas distribution station was built in Bryansk Oblast, in Pogarsky and Starodubsky districts. Gazprom Transgaz Moskva operates the line. An Interfax report on the company's 2025 results and 2030 plans says construction was completed.{w197} An AiF Bryansk article of 22 August 2025, citing the oblast government press service, says the same.{w198}

Both sources give a length of more than 46 kilometers, with 13 valve sites, 6 road and rail crossings and 4 water crossings. No commissioning date, diameter or tie-in point was found. A further connector from Starodub to the Novozybkov station was reported to be in design, with no length given.
P8370: The Tuma to Gus-Khrustalny gas pipeline is a jumper line between Tuma in Ryazan Oblast and Gus-Khrustalny in Vladimir Oblast. A page on the Vladimir linear production department of Gazprom Transgaz Nizhny Novgorod lists it as operating, with a length of 55 kilometers. The page lists it beside another jumper pipeline of 163 kilometers.{w199} The page did not give a diameter, capacity or commissioning year.
P8374:
A 148 kilometer gas pipeline carries gas from the Yarudeyskoye field to a point where it is handed over to Gazprom's transport system. The field has been in commercial production since 2015, and YarGeo operates the pipeline. Two contractor case study pages reprint a YarGeo company profile that gives the 148 kilometer figure.{w200}{w201}

Neither page names the Nadymskaya compressor station. That name and a chainage of 0 to 149 kilometers appear only in the title of a YarGeo construction tender, which could not be read. No diameter, capacity, start year or route was found.
